subtopic: Garbage Collection Mechanics and Memory Leak Profiling
question_text: In a generational garbage collector, what foundational assumption (generational hypothesis) justifies separating objects into young and old generations?

options.text: Old objects consume significantly less memory than young objects
Most allocated objects have very short lifespans and die shortly after creation
Young generation collectors require full application stop-the-world pauses
Thread stacks can only reference old generation objects

answer_explanation: The weak generational hypothesis states that the vast majority of objects die shortly after allocation. Focusing frequent minor collections on the young generation maximizes throughput.
reference_solution: Correct Choice: B. Rationale: The weak generational hypothesis states that the vast majority of objects die shortly after allocation. Focusing frequent minor collections on the young generation maximizes throughput.

criteria.name: Correctness
criteria.description: Selects the exact correct technical option.
